purpose: When will two repeating workshop signals sound together again?
meaning: For positive integers a and b, the least common multiple L is the smallest positive integer divisible by both. If two signals begin together and repeat every a and b minutes, L is their first positive reunion time. Divide ab by their greatest common divisor d to avoid counting the shared factor twice. Signal A and signal B name the two repeating sources; a and b are their minute periods.

definition.setting: Two workshop signals sound together at minute zero. Signal A repeats every a minutes and signal B every b minutes. Choose whole-minute periods and follow their marks along the same timeline. The first shared mark after zero is the next reunion; the cycle counts show how many repetitions each signal completes to get there.

properties.derivation: Write a=d times an integer and b=d times another integer, with the remaining integers coprime. Their smallest shared positive multiple uses both remaining factors and one copy of d, giving ab/d. Each period divides L exactly, so L/a and L/b are whole cycle counts. A separate scan of positive minute marks verifies the first reunion for every allowed pair.
